captions.detailed: A benchtop laboratory monocular microscope featuring a light-grey heavy base and a tall, swept vertical column. It includes a black rectangular specimen stage with sample clips, a black optical body carriage with adjustment knobs, a rotating objective turret with multiple lenses, and an angled monocular viewing tube. The optical body carriage slides vertically on the main column, the specimen stage slides prismatically from left to right, the objective turret rotates continuously, and a small diaphragm lever rotates on a short pivot beneath the stage.
captions.instruction: Create a compact laboratory monocular microscope with a heavy base, a vertical column, a rectangular specimen stage, and an optical body. Ensure the optical carriage can slide vertically, the stage can slide horizontally, the objective turret can rotate continuously, and a diaphragm lever beneath the stage can rotate on a pivot.
captions.factory: Construct the microscope by first building a heavy base and vertical column using extruded profiles with rounded corners. Create the optical body carriage as a sliding block with cylindrical adjustment knobs, and add the angled monocular tube using rotated cylinders. Model the rectangular specimen stage with slim rectangular slides and sample clips, then place a cylindrical condenser housing underneath with a small, rotatable diaphragm lever. Define four joints: a prismatic joint for the vertical carriage movement, a prismatic joint for the horizontal stage movement, a continuous joint for the revolving objective turret, and a revolute joint for the diaphragm lever.
